collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 6-13 and an adult)

collection.description: A child has decided to fish exactly like the kingfisher, from a rock over the stream: let them try, or teach them to watch.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been watching a kingfisher all morning. It sits on a branch over the stream, perfectly still, then drops like a stone into the water and comes up with a fish, every single time. (subject) has decided (subject.he/she) is going to fish exactly the same way. (subject.He/she) is now standing on a rock over the stream, perfectly still, with (subject.his/her) arms tucked in like wings.

choices.label: Teach (subject.him/her) to Watch Like the Kingfisher

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) jumps. There's an enormous splash. (subject.He/she) comes up with no fish, a mouthful of water and a leaf on (subject.his/her) head. The kingfisher flies off in disgust. (friend) is laughing so hard (friend.he/she) has to hold onto a tree. (subject) climbs back onto the rock and jumps again. Same result. They go home wet, fishless, and very happy.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) says the real trick isn't the dive, it's the waiting. They sit on the bank together without moving or talking, watching the water. It's surprisingly hard. (subject) fidgets. Then (subject.he/she) starts seeing things: the shadow of a fish, the way they move in the slow parts. That afternoon (subject.he/she) catches a fish with a little net. (subject.He/she) holds it up to the kingfisher, who doesn't care.
